title: Derived restriction of scalars is termwise
statement:
In the situation of [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat], there is a canonical
isomorphism $R(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)\cong D(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)$ between the
right derived restriction of scalars and the functor
$D(\Mod_{\mathcal S})\to D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ that restricts scalars termwise.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. The ambient hypotheses are those of [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat]: $\mathcal C$ is closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian, tensor is additive in each variable, and $\mathcal R,\mathcal S$ are commutative ring objects. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] separately to $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal R$. Thus $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are Grothendieck abelian; in particular they are abelian. Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] to $\mathcal A$: every cochain complex of $\mathcal S$-modules has a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. This supplies the resolution hypothesis needed for right derivation, without using the K-flat preservation conclusion of the context lemma.

source.place: First sentence: verify the abelian source and target and the right-derived existence hypotheses.

proof.text: Closedness means that $X\otimes-$ has a right adjoint for every $X$. The left-adjoint colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] therefore gives preservation of all existing small colimits by $X\otimes-$. Symmetry gives a natural isomorphism $-\otimes X\cong X\otimes-$; the same colimit universal property is preserved under this isomorphism, so tensoring on either side preserves colimits. The Grothendieck category $\mathcal C$ has equalizers and coequalizers. Hence the hypotheses of clauses 2 and 3 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] hold: it is braided and closed, $\mathcal R$ is commutative, and both tensor functors preserve colimits. Its clause 4 now applies because $\mathcal C$ is abelian and tensor is additive in each variable. It states exactly that $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is exact, preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Its clause 1 identifies $F$ as the unchanged underlying-object and underlying-arrow functor with action restricted through $\varphi$.

source.place: First sentence: exactness of restriction from the change-of-scalars node, with its hypotheses checked.

proof.text: By step 2, $F$ preserves finite colimits between the abelian categories $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$. Thus [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] gives $F(f+g)=F(f)+F(g)$ for every pair of parallel module morphisms. Together with the K-injective resolutions of step 1, this is precisely the additivity and resolution input of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], so $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ is defined. All complexes and derived categories here are unbounded; no boundedness or flatness of $\mathcal S$ over $\mathcal R$ is required.

source.place: Second sentence: check the additive-functor hypotheses of the exact right-derived comparison.

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-right-derived-exact] to this $F$, using step 3 for its right-derived existence hypotheses and step 2 for exactness. It gives the canonical isomorphism $RF\cong D(F)$. By the statement of that node, $D(F)$ is induced by applying $F$ termwise; and clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] identifies this with restriction of the action through $\varphi$ in every degree and on every differential and complex morphism. Substituting $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\mathcal S}$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\mathcal R}$ gives exactly the asserted canonical isomorphism $R(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)\cong D(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)$ between the stated unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Second sentence: specialize the canonical exact-functor comparison to restriction of scalars.

proof_origin.place: Both sentences, expanded using the existing module-category, K-injective-resolution, additivity and exact-derived comparison nodes.
